classification.difficultyReason: Connect constant speed to equal arcs in equal times, then apply the explicitly signposted centre–circumference theorem to explain equal binocular rotations. This requires interpreting the physical situation through routine linked geometric relationships.

content.prompt: (An application of the angle at the centre and circumference theorem) A horse is travelling around a circular track at a constant speed. A punter standing at the very edge of the track is following him with binoculars. Explain why the punter’s binoculars are rotating at a constant rate.

answer.short: In equal times the horse covers equal arcs. Each angle turned through by the binoculars is half the corresponding angle at the centre, so equal times give equal rotations.
answer.worked:
Constant speed around the circular track means the horse covers equal arcs in equal time intervals, giving equal angles at the centre.

For each such arc, the angle through which the punter turns the binoculars is the angle at the circumference, which is half the corresponding angle at the centre. Therefore the binoculars turn through equal angles in equal time intervals and rotate at a constant rate.
